summary.text: CA9 has the strongest convergent evidence in this run. It ranks first in the overall convergence ranking (score 4.52, 5 streams). It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712) and is tumour-intrinsic by single-cell data, where RCC cells hold 0.976 of its tissue transcripts. CA9-targeted PET literature and an antibody in Phase 3 clinical development (girentuximab) support it as both a target and an imaging/tissue biomarker.

CD70 and NNMT complete the top tier. Both are up in tumour at the protein level (log2FC 2.421 and 2.709) and both have ccRCC literature support. CD70 has clinical-stage antibodies and ADCs. NNMT has the clearest prognostic signal among the up-regulated candidates (TCGA Cox log HR 0.301, adjusted p 0.00479) but no drug. In the target profile, SCARB1 (score 4.1314), SLC16A3 and ENPP3 also hold a top-10 position under re-weighting. None of these candidates shows a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines. EPAS1 is the only target examined with a selective, partial dependency (selectivity 0.3), and it has an approved drug (belzutifan).

The biomarker profile is led by PSAT1 (score 4.8696), NNMT (4.7744) and ALDH6A1 (4.7333), all prognostic in TCGA-KIRC. Most strong biomarkers are proximal-tubule genes lost in tumour, such as ALDOB and SLC22A8. In these genes, higher expression tracks better survival (Cox log HR -0.358 and -0.402), so they mark loss of tubule identity rather than offer inhibitor targets.

The main disagreements between layers are these. SCARB1 and ENPP3 are strong in the data but have no ccRCC literature relation in the corpus. A substantial part of SCARB1 expression is endothelial (cpm_share 0.406) rather than tumour (0.194). FCER1G's bulk increase largely disappears when extrapolated to a pure tumour (purity-1 log2FC 1.061), so it is an infiltration signal. VHL is the most recurrent driver (mutation frequency 0.483) and should be read as mechanism, not as a target.

omics.text: The tumour-up tier is concordant across CPTAC RNA and protein. CA9 has RNA log2FC 6.312 and protein log2FC 2.269. NNMT has 4.67 and 2.709, CD70 4.464 and 2.421, SLC16A3 3.435 and 2.279, ENPP3 3.895 and 1.544, and SCARB1 2.974 and 1.837. FABP6 (RNA 4.006, protein 1.921) combines its increase with frequent copy-number gain (frequency 0.573) and a CNV-RNA cis rho of 0.309, consistent with a dosage effect.

The tumour-down tier is dominated by tubule-identity genes. UMOD falls by RNA log2FC -10.31, ALDOB by -7.028 (protein -2.273) and SLC22A8 by -6.715 (protein -2.264). ALDH6A1 (RNA -3.399, protein -1.925) has a dosage-linked loss, with CNV loss frequency 0.355 and cis rho 0.525. These genes are diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, not candidates for inhibition.

literature.text: Published support converges on the same surface antigens. CA9 is described as enriched in ccRCC tumour cells with low background in normal kidney, and CA9 PET gives proof-of-concept non-invasive discrimination of ccRCC. CD70 is described as overexpressed in RCC and minimally expressed in normal tissue, with CD70 single-domain antibody radiotracers in development. NNMT is reported as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target with functional validation, but in a single study. A corpus review title pairs CAIX and CD70 as theranostic targets.

Beyond the top tier, literature support is thinner and mostly bioinformatic. ENO2 has the richest mid-rank support: diagnostic and prognostic claims plus a knockdown study showing reduced glycolysis and induced ferroptosis. SLC6A19 is experimentally tumour-suppressive, which argues against inhibiting it. PSAT1 appears only in a four-gene LASSO-Cox signature, with no extracted relation. SCARB1, ENPP3, FABP6, HK2 and ANGPTL4 have no relation in this small corpus, which is a corpus-coverage gap rather than evidence against them.

external.text: Open Targets and UniProt confirm that the leading up-regulated candidates are accessible membrane proteins. CA9 (association score 0.3088) has tractability up to an approved small-molecule drug and girentuximab in Phase 3. CD70 (association 0.0572, a weak prior) has cusatuzumab in Phase 2 and vorsetuzumab mafodotin in Phase 1. ENPP3 has the ADC AGS-16C3F in Phase 2. SCARB1 has a higher association score (0.4049, genetic association 0.519) but only predicted tractability and no drug.

The established ccRCC targets behave differently from the data-driven ones. EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha, belzutifan approved) shows a selective but partial DepMap dependency: mean effect -0.143 in ccRCC lines, selectivity 0.3, fraction dependent 0.208. MTOR is a strong dependency (mean effect -1.52) but common essential, which implies a narrow therapeutic window. VHL (0.483) and PBRM1 (0.362) are the recurrent drivers and the mechanistic context for HIF-driven CA9 and CD70 induction.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic. In tumour scRNA-seq, RCC cells hold 0.976 of its transcripts (54.7% of RCC cells expressing). Paired by donor against proximal tubule, it has log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189, 6 donors), so the bulk increase is not driven by infiltrating cells.

Several bulk candidates are not purely tumour-intrinsic. SCARB1 is expressed in endothelium (24.5% expressing, cpm_share 0.406) at least as much as in RCC cells (15.5%, cpm_share 0.194). KDR is endothelial (share 0.951) and so an anti-angiogenic microenvironment target. CD74 (macrophage share 0.436) and CXCR4 (CD8 T share 0.563) are immune-compartment genes. MET is mainly tumour-cell (RCC share 0.935). The single-cell records for CD70 and NNMT carry no evidence ids, so their cell-type shares are not quoted. Their purity-extrapolated changes (4.278 and 5.256) support tumour-cell expression.

spatial.text: Spatial context is the weakest layer in this run. The cell agent's Visium neighbourhood finding for CA9 did not pass automatic verification and was removed, so no in-situ enrichment value is reported here. Visium does not cover CD70. The in-situ picture therefore rests on single-cell attribution: CA9 sits in RCC cells (share 0.976), and the SCARB1 signal is partly endothelial (cpm_share 0.406), consistent with a vascular-adjacent component.

structure.text: On CA9, the best molecular-glue-degrader (MGD) site scores 0.546. It is a small pocket (126.8 A3, depth 2.55, mean pLDDT 90.3) with one accessible lysine, and ligand-site recall is 0.5. This ranks a candidate surface for glue design. It is not evidence that a CA9 degrader exists, and antibody or radioligand approaches remain the more mature modality.

Among the discovery candidates, RAB42 has a confident AlphaFold model (mean pLDDT 85.31) and a top MGD site of 0.5348, but the pocket is small (37.4 A3). COL23A1 has a weak model (mean pLDDT 58.91) and a tiny pocket (MGD score 0.2342), so it is not a glue candidate. NNMT and CD70 have no pocket analysis in this run.

discovery.text: COL23A1 is the most promising under-studied candidate in the tumour track (novelty 0.839). RCC cells hold 0.881 of its tumour transcripts. It is up at RNA (log2FC 4.07) and protein (log2FC 2.51), is surface or secreted and antibody-tractable, has low vital-organ expression (max 3 nTPM, heart muscle), and has no clinical drug. That profile makes it a first-in-class antibody hypothesis rather than a small-molecule one.

RAB42 is the second tumour-cell discovery candidate (novelty 0.775). RCC holds 0.627 of its tumour transcripts, it is up at RNA (log2FC 3.11) and protein (log2FC 1.9), and it has only 2 ccRCC papers and no drug. As an intracellular small GTPase, its route would be a small molecule or degrader rather than an antibody.

In the microenvironment tracks, LRRC25 (macrophage share 0.787, novelty 0.704) and GAL3ST4 (macrophage share 0.972) are immune hypotheses, and HMCN1 (endothelial share 0.719) is a stromal one with a modest tumour change. All five discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses. None has dependency or functional evidence, and literature novelty is counted by gene symbol.

validation.text: External replication in TCGA-KIRC is strong for the target tier: CA9 log2FC 9.712, CD70 7.09, ENPP3 5.557 and SCARB1 3.989. Prognosis separates them. NNMT (Cox log HR 0.301, adjusted p 0.00479) and ENO2 (0.364, adjusted p 0.000624) are adverse prognostic markers. CA9 (log HR -0.009) and SCARB1 (-0.038) carry no prognostic signal, so their value is diagnostic and therapeutic rather than prognostic. EPAS1 is prognostic in the favourable direction (log HR -0.381).

Somatic driver status points to VHL (frequency 0.483) and PBRM1 (0.362), not to any of the ranked targets. DepMap weakens every up-regulated candidate as a dependency target: CA9 selectivity is 0.031, CD70 0.006 and SCARB1 -0.021. Only EPAS1 (selectivity 0.3) has a selective, partial dependency. None of the leading candidates is a kinase with a protein-adjusted activity score, so the kinase layer adds nothing to them. Their case rests on surface accessibility (antigen, ADC or radioligand), not on tumour-cell essentiality.

The purity check strengthens the tumour-intrinsic candidates. CA9 rises from 6.312 to 7.787 when extrapolated to a pure tumour, NNMT reaches 5.256 and ENPP3 5.278. It exposes infiltration signals: FCER1G drops from 2.499 to 1.061 (purity rho -0.692), TYROBP from 2.692 to 1.196 (rho -0.729), and FCGR3A has rho -0.65. These are immune markers, not tumour targets. ALDH6A1's loss shrinks from -3.399 to -1.973 at purity 1, so part of its bulk decrease reflects normal-tissue admixture.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the target profile, seven candidates keep a top-10 position: SCARB1 (P top-10 0.968, rank interval 1 to 8), CA9 (0.941), SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 and NNMT (0.88 each), ENPP3 (0.823) and FABP6 (0.803). In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is robust (P top-10 0.894, interval 1 to 15). VHL depends heavily on the weights (interval up to 580), as does PIGR (up to 56).

In the biomarker profile, PSAT1 (P top-10 0.96), NNMT (0.973) and ALDH6A1 (0.808) are robust. ALDOB (0.493, interval up to 99) and SLC22A8 (0.441, interval up to 194) are weight-dependent, even though both sit near the top of the overall ranking. Their biomarker position relies on the omics weight more than on replication or prognosis.

integration.text: Omics, literature, external knowledge and cell context converge fully on CA9 and nearly fully on CD70. Both are tumour-intrinsic, replicated, membrane-accessible and clinically targeted, and both lack a dependency. NNMT converges on omics, literature and prognosis but lacks drugs and a dependency, which makes it a prognostic biomarker with a hypothesis-level target case. SCARB1 and ENPP3 are where the data run ahead of the literature. PSAT1 is where the layers conflict: it is lower in tumour yet higher expression predicts worse survival.

The candidates fall into three groups. Targets: CA9, CD70, ENPP3, SCARB1, SLC16A3 and the established EPAS1. Biomarkers: PSAT1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB, SLC22A8 and ENO2, plus NNMT and CA9 in a dual role. Mechanism and context: VHL and PBRM1 as drivers, SLC6A19 as a tumour suppressor, and FCER1G, TYROBP and KDR as microenvironment genes whose bulk signal reflects infiltrating or stromal cells.

targets.rationale: First in the overall ranking (score 4.52) and the only robust overall top-10 gene (P top-10 0.894). Up at RNA (6.312) and protein (2.269), replicated in TCGA (9.712), rising to 7.787 at purity 1, and 0.976 of transcripts in RCC cells. Girentuximab is in Phase 3 and CA9 PET has proof-of-concept literature. It is not prognostic (log HR -0.009) and not a dependency (selectivity 0.031), so its value is as an antigen and imaging target.

Up at RNA (4.464) and protein (2.421), replicated in TCGA (7.09) and tumour-intrinsic at purity 1 (4.278), with target-profile P top-10 0.88. Literature supports it as a target and as an imaging marker, and cusatuzumab and vorsetuzumab mafodotin are clinical-stage. TCGA prognosis is not significant (log HR 0.126, adjusted p 0.175).

The only candidate robust in both profiles: biomarker score 4.7744 (P top-10 0.973) and target P top-10 0.88. Up at protein (2.709), purity-robust (5.256), and adversely prognostic (log HR 0.301, adjusted p 0.00479). Ranked above SCARB1 because its literature and prognosis agree with the omics. The target case rests on one study and there is no dependency (selectivity -0.075).

Up at RNA (3.895) and protein (1.544), replicated in TCGA (5.557), tumour-intrinsic at purity 1 (5.278), and robust in the target profile (P top-10 0.823). The ADC AGS-16C3F reached Phase 2. Placed above SCARB1 for clinical precedent despite having no literature relation in the corpus.

Top of the target profile (4.1314, P top-10 0.968), with Open Targets association 0.4049 (genetic 0.519). Up at RNA (2.974) and protein (1.837), replicated in TCGA (3.989). Ranked below the numeric order because single-cell data place much of its expression in endothelium (cpm_share 0.406 vs 0.194 in RCC), it has no ccRCC literature or drug, and it has no dependency.

Included despite overall rank 38 because it is the only candidate with a selective DepMap dependency (mean effect -0.143, selectivity 0.3, fraction dependent 0.208, adjusted p 0.061) and an approved drug (belzutifan). Expression with protein log2FC 1.162 is modest, and higher expression tracks better survival (log HR -0.381). It is a validated pathway target rather than an expression-driven one.

MCT4 lactate transporter, robust in the target profile (P top-10 0.881). Up at RNA (3.435) and protein (2.279), replicated in TCGA (3.291), rising to 3.821 at purity 1 with cis rho 0.258. The purity data argue for tumour-cell expression, against the literature agent's microenvironment caveat. There is no drug or dependency.

Top of the biomarker profile (4.8696, P top-10 0.96). Down at RNA (-3.867) and protein (-1.963) and replicated in TCGA (-2.974), yet higher expression predicts worse survival (log HR 0.43, adjusted p 5.66e-7). This direction paradox and the lack of literature relations make it a strong but unexplained prognostic marker.

Robust in the biomarker profile (4.7333, P top-10 0.808), with the strongest prognostic signal (log HR -0.554, adjusted p 9.45e-12): lower expression tracks worse survival. CNV dosage supports it (cis rho 0.525). Its purity-1 change is smaller (-1.973 vs -3.399), so part of the bulk loss is normal admixture.

Second in the overall ranking, down at RNA (-7.028) and protein (-2.273), replicated in TCGA (-4.741), with IHC and bioinformatic literature. Higher expression tracks better survival (log HR -0.358, adjusted p 0.000023). Ranked below PSAT1 and ALDH6A1 because its biomarker position is weight-dependent (P top-10 0.493).

Up at RNA (3.538) and protein (2.245), replicated in TCGA (3.085), purity-robust (4.561), and adversely prognostic (log HR 0.364, adjusted p 0.000624). Several studies support it, including a knockdown that reduced glycolysis. It has no tractability evidence, so it stays a biomarker.

OAT3, strongly down at RNA (-6.715) and protein (-2.264) and replicated in TCGA (-6.154). Higher expression tracks better survival (log HR -0.402, adjusted p 0.0000433), and methylation literature supports it. Ranked last because its biomarker position is the most weight-dependent (P top-10 0.441).

limitations.text: No leading up-regulated candidate shows a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines. Target calls rest on surface accessibility and clinical precedent, not on tumour-cell essentiality.

The literature graph covers a few hundred ccRCC abstracts, so missing relations (SCARB1, ENPP3, FABP6, PSAT1) reflect corpus coverage. Most prognostic literature claims are single-study TCGA bioinformatics.
The Visium spatial finding for CA9 failed automatic verification and was dropped, and one literature finding was also dropped. Spatial context is therefore not part of the conclusions.
Single-cell shares come from few donors for some cell groups, and CD70 and NNMT have no evidence-linked single-cell records.
MGD scores rank candidate pockets only. No molecular glue is known for any candidate, and discovery candidates are untested hypotheses.

Clinical-stage drug information comes from Open Targets records, not from trial outcomes. This is replicate run rep2 of the pipeline, and the subagents worked mainly from convergence-ranking rows rather than per-gene re-queries.
